title: MEXT-Designated Preparatory Courses: What They Fix and Who Runs Them
summary: A designated preparatory course is not a better Japanese class. It is the only thing that closes a schooling-years gap, and the designated list is short.
body_html:
If your prior schooling runs fewer than 12 years, you cannot enter a Japanese university on it — and no amount of Japanese study changes that. [source:1] What changes it is completing a designated preparatory education course. [source:1]

That word, designated, is the whole thing. It is a ministry designation held by specific named courses at specific named institutions, published as a list. [source:2] A school without it cannot close the gap, however it describes its curriculum.

What the designation does, precisely

The rule is 12 years of regular school education abroad. [source:1] Where the completed course is fewer than 12 years, you must additionally complete a designated preparatory education course or a designated training institution course. [source:1]

Note the word "additionally". The preparatory course does not replace your schooling — it is added on top of it. You are not making up the missing years in the abstract; you are completing a course that the ministry accepts as closing that specific gap.

This is also why it cannot be substituted. A JLPT certificate proves Japanese ability. An entrance exam score proves academic readiness. Neither of them is a designated course, so neither of them makes you eligible.

The list is not what people expect

Two assumptions tend to be wrong.

It is not just language schools. University-attached centres hold the designation too — the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies international student Japanese language education centre, and the Osaka University Japanese language and culture education centre. [source:2] So do the Japan Student Services Organization's own Tokyo and Osaka Japanese language education centres. [source:2]

If you would rather do your preparatory year inside a university environment than at a language school, that option exists and is rarely presented.

It is a short list. The ministry publishes it with an as-of date, and entries carry their own applicability dates. [source:2] Several rows are historical — they apply only to people who entered the course between two given dates. [source:2] So an institution appearing on the page is not the same as that course being open to you now.

Read the remarks column before anything else. A course that stopped accepting students years ago still appears, because the list is a record of designations rather than a prospectus.

Which of the schools we cover hold it

Two of them, and both appear on the ministry's current list.

Sendagaya Japanese School, in Shinjuku. [source:2] Its preparatory education course runs 2 years from an April start and 1 year 6 months from October, with intakes in April and October and a stated capacity of 1,728. [source:3] The school states that only around 30 schools nationwide hold the accreditation. [source:3]

Akamonkai Japanese Language School's main school, in Arakawa. [source:2] It describes its preparatory course as the ministry-designated course for people whose secondary education runs to fewer than 12 years, to obtain the qualification to enter a Japanese university, running 1 year 6 months or 2 years. [source:4]

Both descriptions match the ministry's list, which is the useful part: you can check a school's claim against a government page rather than taking its word.

How to verify a claim yourself

This matters because the designation is valuable and the wording around it gets loose. "Preparation course", "university preparation programme" and "preparatory education course" are not interchangeable — only the last one, as designated, has legal effect on your eligibility.

  • Open the ministry's list and search for the institution name. [source:2] If it is not there, it does not hold the designation.
  • Check the course name, not just the institution. The designation attaches to a named course. [source:2]
  • Check the remarks column for date restrictions. [source:2]
  • Check the as-of date on the list itself. [source:2] A designation can be added or withdrawn between revisions.
  • Ask the school, in writing, to confirm that the course you are being offered is the designated one. A school that holds the designation will answer this instantly.

Before you commit to a preparatory year

Make sure you actually need one. There are other routes to eligibility that do not involve an extra course — a designated 11-year course list, and recognition of schools accredited by international bodies. [source:1] If one of those applies to you, a preparatory year is a year and a tuition bill you did not need to spend.

And confirm your own schooling first. The ministry says explicitly that whether your course was regular school education, and which year of it you completed, is a question for your country's embassy. [source:1] Get that answer before you enrol anywhere, because it determines whether this entire article applies to you.

The full set of eligibility routes is laid out in do you actually qualify for a Japanese university. For how one designated course sits alongside its sibling schools, see the Sendagaya group comparison, and for the other designated school we cover, Akamonkai compared with ISI. Profiles: Sendagaya Japanese School, Akamonkai.

The designated list is maintained by the Ministry of Education and revised; course structures are set by the schools and carry effective-from dates. The pages linked below are the authority. We prepare and forward application documents — eligibility is determined by the institution you apply to, not by us.

claims_without_sources: 指定課程の現行校数 —— 文科省は「◯校」という数え方をしていない。千駄ヶ谷が自校ページで「約30校」と述べている点は出典付きで引いたが、こちらで行を数えた数は書いていない。一覧には適用期間が限定された歴史的な行が多数含まれており、単純な行数は現行校数と一致しない。
収録校以外で指定を持つ学校の評価・比較 —— 一覧に載っている他校（大原日本語学院、KCP、新宿日本語学校など）は本サイトが未収録で、課程内容を確認していないため、名前を挙げての比較はしていない。大学附属センターと日本学生支援機構のセンターのみ、「語学学校以外にもある」という論点に必要なので挙げた。
指定が取り消される条件・頻度 —— 文科省は一覧に as-of 日付を付けているが、追加・取消の基準や頻度を公表していない。「改定の間に変わりうる」とだけ書いた。
準備教育課程を経た場合の進学実績 —— どの学校も公表していない。
研修施設課程（準備教育課程とは別の指定）の中身 —— 一覧の存在は出典どおりだが、別一覧の内容を確認していないため、経路として言及するに留めた。
